title: Jolina Reinhold: 17-Jährige mit Olympia-Ambitionen
snippet: Jolina Reinhold ist bereits U18-Weltmeisterin. Bei den Jugendspielen in Dakar hofft die 17-jährige Judoka auf die nächste Goldmedaille – und träumt von Olympia 2028.

title: Zverev: "Wichtigste Person in meinem Leben"
snippet: Als Nummer eins der Weltrangliste widmet Alexander Zverev seiner Mutter bewegende Worte. Sie stand ihm auch nach der Diabetes-Diagnose zur Seite und glaubte stets an seine Träume.

title: Das Sport-Wochenende: Klassiker und jüngster F1-Weltmeister
snippet: Die Bundesliga bot ein Unentschieden im Spitzenspiel und einen beachtlichen Rekord durch Niko Ilicevic. Die Youth Olympic Games haben begonnen und Kimi Antonelli ist Weltmeister.

title: Klimaaktivistin Neubauer: Gewaltdebatte "gefundenes Fressen"
snippet: Nach den Gen-Z-Demos überlagere die Gewaltdebatte die Inhalte der Protestierenden, kritisiert Aktivistin Neubauer. Ministerin Prien fordert eine Politik für alle Generationen.

title: Jüdische Akademie: Eröffnung mit Frank-Walter Steinmeier
snippet: Rede von Frank-Walter Steinmeier (Bundespräsident, SPD) zur Eröffnung der Jüdischen Akademie in Frankfurt

title: AfD: Deutsch-russische und deutsch-amerikanische Beziehungen
snippet: AfD-Pressekonferenz zu deutsch-russischen und deutsch-amerikanischen Beziehungen mit Markus Frohnmaier (AfD, stellv. Fraktionsvorsitzender), Stefan Keuter (AfD, stellv. Fraktionsvorsitzender) und Gerold Otten (stellvertretender Sprecher des AK Außen)

title: Digitalgipfel: Eröffnung mit Karsten Wildberger
snippet: Eröffnung des Digitalgipfels 2026 mit einer Rede von Karsten Wildberger (CDU, Digitalminister)

title: Gefährliches Vorhofflimmern erkennen und behandeln
snippet: Über 1,6 Millionen Menschen in Deutschland sind von Vorhofflimmern betroffen. Unbehandelt kann die Herzrhythmusstörung schwere Folgen haben. Welche Warnzeichen man kennen sollte.

title: Im Kopf von Patrice Aminati
snippet: Patrice Aminati ist unheilbar krank – und will leben. Im Psychologie-Talk mit Leon Windscheid erzählt sie, was der Krebs ihr abverlangt – und wie Glaube und kleine Genuss-Momente ihr Kraft geben.

title: Im Kopf von Jihan Alomar
snippet: Als Kind wurde Jihan Alomar vom IS verschleppt. Leon Windscheid erzählt sie, wie das Trauma ihr Leben prägt – und warum sie sich nach ihrer Flucht auch in Deutschland nicht sicher fühlt.

title: Trump, US midterms, Tehran: 8 key factors driving Iran war
snippet: While the US midterms could open a window for diplomacy with Iran, they could also unleash a new military escalation. DW spoke to analysts to identify eight factors that could tip the balance towards war or peace.

title: Ice hockey officials considering options after CAS order to reinstate Russia
snippet: Ice hockey's ruling body is deciding how to respond to a decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport that allows Russia back into international competition. Germany hasn't ruled out pulling out as a tournament host.

title: European supermarkets targeted in second reported cyberattack
snippet: Supermarkets across Europe have been targeted in cyberattacks once again. Three weeks after a defrosting attack in France, supermarkets in Belgium, Estonia, Ireland, Luxembourg and Sweden reported freezer malfunctions.

title: LA communities kick out Big Oil
snippet: After years of advocacy from residents and legal battles with Big Oil, LA has voted to ban drilling and phase out oil extraction in the city. It's the first city in the country to kick the oil industry out.

title: Germany's chancellor called for Korean unity. Does Seoul want that?
snippet: Germany, like Korea, was once divided by rival political systems and by one of the world's most fortified borders. Chancellor Merz called for a reunified Korea during his recent visit — but the prospect seems faint.

title: Global pedestrian Karl Bushby returns home to UK after 28-year trek
snippet: Karl Bushby, a British man who traveled 50,000 km without transport over the past 28 years, has come home. Starting in Chile, he crossed the Americas, Russia and parts of Central Asia and Europe — almost all on foot.

title: Uganda begins withdrawing troops from Somalia after two decades
snippet: Ugandan troops first deployed to Somalia in 2007 as part of an international military coalition to battle Islamic insurgents. But the mission has faced mounting pressure since a US decision to withdraw funding.

title: How Iliana Yotova won the presidential election in Bulgaria
snippet: Iliana Yotova won the presidential election in Bulgaria, promising to be a "president of peace." But the campaign showed how divided Bulgarians are about the war in Ukraine and drone attacks in the Black Sea.

title: Will renewed conflict derail Ethiopia's economic growth?
snippet: Ethiopia's economy is growing strongly. But renewed fighting in the north of the BRICS member state could deter investment, strain public finances and push up the cost of living.

title: For US Democrats, climate policy is now about energy bills
snippet: Climate change has all but disappeared from Democrats' campaign pitches, replaced by promises to lower electricity bills. So what would the party really do for climate policy should it win control of Congress?

title: US: 9 killed in Florida jet crash
snippet: A Learjet plane crashed near a busy road in a residential neighborhood in Palm Beach County, leaving all nine people on board dead and a large crater on ground.

title: Germany news: Berlin hosts digital summit with AI focus
snippet: A government-run conference is to look at the uses and dangers of artificial intelligence. This comes as the German and UK defense ministers will discuss expanding AI's role in military cooperation. DW has more.

title: Serbia: Police chief arrested for abuse of office
snippet: Marko Kricak, an Aleksandar Vucic loyalist, is accused of suppressing and manipulating an investigation into a gangland murder. Prosecutors say the arrest is not linked to Vucic's recent election defeat.

title: Setomaa kindergarten holds its own Olympics in Värska
snippet: While older kids were off school for fall break last week, Setomaa kindergarteners gathered at Värska School for a day of Olympic-inspired sports and games.

title: Tallinn's ice skating rinks begin new season
snippet: Ice skating season has begun in Tallinn after several municipal-run rinks opened their doors over the weekend, with more expected to do so in the coming weeks.

title: Therapist: No skills needed to benefit from creative arts therapy
snippet: Creative arts therapy can help people of all ages express emotions and memories beyond words, with no artistic skills required, Estonian therapist Epp Sussen says.

title: Tallinn bench marks birthplace of iconic Estonian novel 'Truth and Justice'
snippet: A commemorative bench by Tallinn Central Hospital now marks the place where Estonian author A. H. Tammsaare penned his classic "Truth and Justice," first published in 1926.

title: Võro-language Minecraft, Zumba and film marathon on tap for language week
snippet: Starting Monday, Võro Language Week will celebrate the regional Southeastern Estonian language with events from a Minecraft session to a Zumba class — all in Võro.

title: Russian citizen expelled to 'prevent activities' that 'threaten' Estonia
snippet: A Russian citizen was expelled from Estonia on Monday who had links to the Russian security services, Estonia's Internal Security Service (KAPO) said. The individual was a professor at the now-closed Euroacademy in Tallinn and also worked at ERR for two years.

title: Defense Forces broke law on Ukrainian soldier training background checks
snippet: The Estonian Defense Forces (EDF) acted illegally when it barred a reservists from taking part in a military exercise due to his criminal record, the Justice Chancellor ruled.

title: Hackers raised freezer temperature at Selver supermarket to +50°C
snippet: A cyber attack hit a Selver supermarket in Estonia, with hackers accessing a computer controlling refrigeration and changing a freezer setting to 50 degrees above zero.

title: Saaremaa ferry boss jailed over €4m insolvency begins prison term
snippet: Vjatšeslav Leedo, convicted of causing the insolvency of a ferry serving Estonia's islands, has started serving his sentence in Tallinn Prison.

title: Retired officer: Russian mass strikes unlikely to break Ukrainian resolve
snippet: Russia's attack on a passenger train in Dnipro was a war crime, but such strikes rarely break a population's will to resist, said retired Estonian Brig. Gen. Alar Laneman.

title: Why is Narva's C1 Estonian exam pass rate half the national average?
snippet: Only 14.9 percent of candidates passed September's C1 Estonian exam in the eastern border town of Narva, compared with 29.3 percent nationwide.

title: Second-pillar fund withdrawers can start saving again this month
snippet: People who withdrew their second-pillar pension savings following reforms can, five years on, start contributing again from this month, and experts urge them to do so.

title: Tartu's Christmas village takes shape ahead of First Advent opening
snippet: Tartu is once again transforming Town Hall Square for the holidays, with an outdoor ice rink, Christmas tree and festive pavilions set to open November 29.

title: Põltsamaa school hires security amid ongoing student disruptions
snippet: Põltsamaa Basic School is bringing in security patrols and equipping staff with panic buttons after repeated disruptions by a small group of students.

title: Skater Niina Petrõkina sets PB to take silver in Canada
snippet: Estonian figure skater Niina Petrõkina set a new personal best and finished second at the Grand Prix stage in Kelowna, British Columbia.

title: Soomaa farmers lose 150 cattle to wolves as court blocks hunting permit
snippet: Farmers in Soomaa in southwest Estonia have been facing wolf attacks on livestock as well as bears destroying feed. Hunting permits were suspended soon after being issued.

title: Latvia's insolvent Valka stops cooperation programs with Estonia's Valga
snippet: Cross-border cooperation projects between Estonia's Valga and Latvia's Valka have been suspended as the Latvian municipality is insolvent and must undergo a financial restructuring process.

title: Tartu's 'self-service bar' scrutinized over underage and takeout drinking fears
snippet: A Tartu bar where no staff work on site and drinks are bought from vending machines is being investigated by the city government, over whether it complies with alcohol laws, Tartu Postimees reported.

title: Why are laundromats becoming more popular in Tallinn?
snippet: In Estonia, it is generally not customary to wash one's dirty laundry in public, but suddenly a whole string of self-service laundromats has appeared in Tallinn. Although there are hardly any homes without a washing machine, ERR investigated why people no longer want to do their own laundry at home.

snippet: Une attaque similaire avait touché la France mi-octobre. "Il s'agit d'une tentative délibérée de perturber notre chaîne d'approvisionnement alimentaire et de saper la confiance des consommateurs", a réagi le commissaire européen à l'Agriculture.

snippet: Les mesures proposées par l'exécutif n'ont pas convaincu les jeunes présents lundi devant l'établissement. "On arrêtera de se mobiliser quand le gouvernement arrêtera juste d'essayer de nous faire plaisir avec des mesures bidon", a martelé l'un des organisateurs du blocus.

snippet: Le déstockage de 10 millions de barils de gazole issus de réserves stratégiques commence à entraîner une baisse des tarifs dans les stations-service. Cette ristourne à la pompe sera cependant éphémère, prévient le gouvernement.

title: Midterms 2026 : une campagne électorale marquée par une avalanche de fausses informations
snippet: Accusations de fraudes électorales, vidéos de campagne générées par intelligence artificielle, attaques mensongères contre des candidats... Les élections de mi-mandat vont débuter mardi aux Etats-Unis et les fausses informations se multiplient sur les réseaux sociaux.

title: Une pétition appelant à fermer la chaîne CNews dépasse 500 000 signatures sur le site de l'Assemblée nationale, seuil requis pour un possible débat
snippet: Pour cela, toutefois, une commission doit auparavant se prononcer en décidant de la classer ou de l'examiner, élaborant alors ce rapport.

title: Les Etats-Unis approuvent la version générique d'un traitement préventif contre le VIH, nouvel espoir pour de nombreux pays
snippet: Le traitement sera disponible dans 120 Etats au prix de 40 dollars par personne et par an, avec deux injections. L'organisation Unitaid a salué "une avancée extraordinaire pour la santé mondiale".

title: Le skipper Francis Joyon a été victime d'un chavirage sur la Route du Rhum, une opération de secours déclenchée

title: "Je suis dans la même forme qu'avant" : ce qu'il faut retenir de la conférence de presse de Sophie Adenot après son programme de récupération
snippet: Après trois semaines passées à Cologne, l'astronaute française était de retour au siège de l'ESA à Paris pour une conférence de presse. "Ça va très bien", a-t-elle assuré, admettant aussi que "l'esprit met du temps à se réadapter".

title: La municipalité de Lodève, dans l'Hérault, porte plainte après des inscriptions racistes sur une mosquée
snippet: Mardi dernier, des inscriptions racistes et menaçantes ont été retrouvées sur la boîte aux lettres de la mosquée de la ville, telles que "Islam dehors" et "la valise ou le cercueil".

title: Mairie de Limoges incendiée : un million d'euros de dons déjà récoltés pour sa reconstruction
snippet: Cette cagnotte, ouverte par la Fondation du patrimoine, atteignait plus d'un million d'euros de dons lundi à la mi-journée, de la part de plus de 9 000 donateurs.

title: Le père de Pengo Bossio Wangi, tué dans l'attentat dans les Yvelines, souhaite que l'hommage national permette une "prise de conscience" contre le racisme

title: Le prix Médicis 2026 est décerné à Philippe Vasset pour son roman "Dans les grandes lignes"
